findings.title: HyperCore sends unsigned transfers in the name of addresses that never signed, including a contract, and the record that names such an address is outside the deployer's documented action
findings.difference: HyperCore places system transactions in HyperEVM blocks without a signature and states their sender itself, and the replay client takes that sender from the s value with no check. Under AQAv2 a token's linked contract and a treasury address designated by the treasury deployer rebalance supply. On Ethereum a balance leaves an address only through a transaction it signed or a call made by its own code.
findings.mechanism: If HyperCore named the PoolManager as the treasury address of an aligned quote asset, a system transaction with the PoolManager as sender could move that token out of the PoolManager outside any unlock. sync stores the balance at the time of the call and _settle credits only the increase within one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365), so pool state and ERC-6909 claims would still count the moved tokens as owed, and the last takes in that token would fail in the transfer of src/types/Currency.sol. This cycle added evidence that the path has not been used and found nothing that settles who can name the address. In 18,502 more blocks (52,332,899 to 52,351,400) all 9,135 gas price 0 transactions came from the 54 known system senders, none named the PoolManager, and the PoolManager nonce is still 1 on four endpoints. The exchange endpoint page is byte identical to the cycle 26 copy, and authorizeAqav2Role still takes token and role only.
findings.impact: All pools and ERC-6909 claims in a token for which HyperCore named the PoolManager as the rebalancing address. Nothing is exposed today.
findings.preconditions: The treasury deployer of an aligned quote asset (two staked deployers of 500,000 HYPE) must designate the PoolManager, and activation needs a validator vote. An ordinary account can do neither.
findings.mitigations: Watch the PoolManager nonce, which rises with any system transaction sent in its name. Ask Hyperliquid whether the node refuses an address with EVM code as AQAv2 treasury.

No arithmetic, comparison, shift, MULMOD, ADDMOD, 512 bit mulDiv, KECCAK256, MCOPY, CALLDATALOAD or JUMPI vector differs, so FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14), TickMath, SqrtPriceMath and SwapMath compute the Ethereum words through this endpoint.

cleared.check: Transient storage journal on frame revert, nested revert, STATICCALL and account isolation (9 vectors) on mainnet, the f0cad31 replica and testnet.
cleared.result: All 9 return the specified word. CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39), NonzeroDeltaCount (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32), CurrencyReserves and Lock (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25) rely on a reverted frame dropping its TSTORE and on per-account slots; both hold, so a hook or router that catches a reverted PoolManager call cannot keep a delta or lock change from it, and unlock's NonzeroDeltaCount check (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) sees the true count.

leads.question: Which hl-node build did the 2026-11-16 compatibility reminder for nanoreth answer to, and did it change any EVM execution rule, given that nanoreth tag nb-20261125-2 and master pin the same revm as before?
leads.why: A validator change that needed replay clients to update would be the one place where the closed validator's execution could have moved away from the public replicas.

leadResults.answer: The 50 newest blocks with PoolManager Swap or ModifyLiquidity logs (50,978,353 to 52,134,672, one transaction each) wrote 552 PoolManager slots. The prestateTracer diff on rpc.purroofgroup.com, eth_getStorageAt on both replicas at the block and eth_getStorageAt on all three endpoints at head agree on every slot: 0 differences. Two slots were rewritten later and still agree at head. No later PoolManager write exists to compare (out/l1193.json).

Operator or issuer level. The exchange endpoint and aligned quote assets pages are byte identical to cycle 26 and 28, so authorizeAqav2Role still names no address and no published check of the treasury's code exists. 18,502 more blocks show only the 54 known system senders for gas price 0 transactions and none to or as the PoolManager, whose nonce is still 1. F-020 stays plausible, operator, high, out of scope.

No page publishes the producer's admission rule for gas price 0 transactions; the only doc change is a sentence on RPC server latency. The census of blocks 52,332,899 to 52,351,400 shows 9,135 gas price 0 transactions, all from system senders.

Follow mode could not run on a live write: the PoolManager emitted no Swap or ModifyLiquidity log after block 52,134,672 and only Initialize logs up to 52,266,493. The L-1193 comparison of 552 written slots stands in for it; a replacement lead is recorded.
